new_statements.rule_in_words: Naawa is described (preliminarily) as having a word-level tone system of the Sherpa type, i.e. a lexical tone/register contrast anchored on the word with the pitch melody realised over the first two syllables (peak/melody on the second syllable). No statement about word stress or accent placement is made anywhere in the article.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the author calls the comparison 'preliminary' and notes (p.54) that no descriptive grammar of Naawa exists.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level tone (by analogy with Watters' analysis of Sherpa); no phrase-level or citation-form detail given.
new_statements.identity_note: Condra's 'Naawa' = Glottolog Naaba naab1241 / ISO nao (also Naapa, Nawa Sherpa, Nage); his data come from Kimathangka and Dangok villages (NE Sankhuwasabha) and diaspora speakers in Khandbari/Kathmandu. Not to be confused with Gur 'naaba' (Mooré royal title) hits or the Ghanaian surname Naawa that dominate bibliographic searches.
